thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV1 paging: GPU capacity exhaustion in eu-west-1. Autoscaler not keeping up, inference queue growth detected (inference-queue-ml > 11k). Root alert at 4943216789. Paging oncall-sre.

Riley (oncall-sre): Ack. Triage note: HPA not scaling due to missing custom metrics from prometheus-adapter. Will gather quick facts.

Maya (infra): Observed spike in prometheus-adapter latency and 5xxs. metrics-server is fine. Prom-adapter logs show repeated timeouts to prometheus and several OOMKilled pods in last 10m.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Model-serving pool at 100% GPU memory; some replicas stuck in CrashLoopBackOff during warmup. We also hit ``maxReplicas`` limit on the GPU HPA (configured 60).

Lia (eng-ml): Customer impact: hosted api p95 latency increased ~4x for smaller models (gpt-medium-quant) — enterprise reserved capacity unaffected. Some low-priority customers seeing 503s after queue timeout.

Riley (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation checklist: 1) Pause any noncritical GPU batch jobs. 2) Restart prometheus-adapter to clear its internal queue. 3) Temporarily change HPA metric source to metrics-server fallback. 4) Increase GPU nodepool by +5 if cloud quota allows. 5) Apply routing policy to shift non-enterprise traffic to cpu-quant variant.

Ops Manager (ops): Julie, please draft an interim message for impacted customers. Avoid technical details, mention "performance degradation" and ETA for next update.

Julie (customer-success): Draft ready: "We're investigating increased latency for inference requests in eu-west-1. We're applying mitigations now and will follow up in 30 minutes." Will send once we confirm mitigation steps. :white_check_mark:

Jonah (eng-runtime): Running commands to confirm state:

```bash
kubectl -n models get hpa -o wide
kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter --tail=300
kubectl top pods -n models --containers | grep -i gpu
```

Riley (oncall-sre): `kubectl describe hpa model-serving-gpu` shows no recent metric samples for 6m. prometheus-adapter logs include "error fetching series" and spike in scrape_time_seconds. Looks like prom queries are heavy or adapter resrc starved.

Maya (infra): Kicking a rolling restart of prometheus-adapter now. Also checking nodepool soft limits; cloud shows we have +7 available GPUs. Proceeding to scale by +5.

registry-bot: Notice: Excessive image pulls detected for model shards. Throttling may apply.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Noted. We've seen image pull rate limits causing pods to be delayed during scale-up. Will stagger pulls and increase imagePullPolicy concurrency.

Riley (oncall-sre): Patched HPA to use fallback metric from metrics-server (queue_length) so autoscaler can act while adapter recovers. Patch command executed.

Lia (eng-ml): Recommend conservative maxReplicas bump to 85 while backlog clears, to avoid hitting hard cap during recovery. Confirm change?

Riley (oncall-sre): Approve bump to 85 temporarily. Applying now.

Maya (infra): Nodepool scale request accepted; nodes provisioning (ETA ~4m). prometheus-adapter restarted; post-restart logs look better, error rates dropping.

Jonah (eng-runtime): K8s started spinning up new replicas. However, several pods failed image pull due to registry quota throttling. I'm enabling a temporary fallback to cached images and increasing image pull concurrency: updating daemon config.

Lia (eng-ml): Routing policy to offload non-enterprise traffic to cpu-quant model applied. Config snippet (in-channel):

```json
{"routing": {"match": "customer.tier != 'enterprise'","target": "gpt-medium-cpu-quant","grace": 45}}
```

Ops Manager (ops): Julie, send the customer note now with the routing action mentioned as "temporary measures to prioritize critical workloads".

Julie (customer-success): Sent. Getting back two support tickets already; adding them to incident tracker.

Riley (oncall-sre): Monitoring metrics: queue length moving from 11.2k -> 6.6k after scale-up and rerouting. p95 latency trending down but still ~1.7x baseline.

Maya (infra): Nodepool +5 completed. GPU utilization dropped to ~88% across pool. No further OOMs observed since prometheus-adapter restart.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Some pods repeatedly crash on startup due to missing local shard files; increasing startup concurrency causes registry hiccups. Implemented staggered start and pre-pulled images on two nodes. Should reduce pull storms.

registry-bot: Action taken: pre-pulled image:gpt-medium-quant:v2 on nodes node-a,node-b.

Lia (eng-ml): Post-mitigation impact: approx 12% of requests in eu-west-1 hit >10s latency window. Majority of enterprise traffic remained within SLA.

Riley (oncall-sre): Next actions: 1) Patch prometheus-adapter to avoid heavy query path (Jonah will PR). 2) Add alert if HPA receives no new metrics for >90s. 3) Update runbook for metrics-adapter OOM scenarios. 4) Cloud: request permanent quota increase for GPU pool.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Opening PR #3592 to guard against nil pointer in adapter and increase adapter resources. Adding unit tests for heavy query edge case.

Maya (infra): Filing cloud support ticket for quota bump; also scheduling a controlled test to exercise autoscaler with synthetic load next week.

Ops Manager (ops): Schedule incident review in 48 hours. Julie, assemble customer impact log and affected tickets.

Julie (customer-success): Will compile and attach to the postmortem.

Riley (oncall-sre): Current state: queue length ~3.1k and falling. Latency p95 closer to 1.2x baseline. Moving to recovery and handing off monitoring to night oncall.

incident-bot: Incident state updated: RECOVERING. Notifying incident-review, eng-runtime, infra.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Handoff notes: saw adapter stacktrace `panic: nil pointer deref` at queryHandler.go:142. PR #3592 addresses this and tunes concurrency. Also note image registry rate limits causing pod start delays; consider mirroring images to regional registry.

Riley (oncall-sre): Handoff to Maya (infra) for the next 2 hours. Attaching emergency steps to ticket and runbook updates.

Maya (infra): Acknowledged. Will monitor and coordinate follow-ups.

Lia (eng-ml): I'll prepare tuning for kv-cache warmup to reduce initial GPU memory pressure.

Ops Manager (ops): Great work team. Make sure all action items have owners in the incident ticket. We'll review in the RCA meeting. :white_check_mark:
